drivingQuestion: Is the storekeeper liable when only the homeowner, not the agent, remembered?
outcomeNote: contradiction resolved in the next unit

segments.he: שִׁלַּח בְּיַד פִּקֵּחַ וְכוּ׳. וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִידְּכַר שָׁלִיחַ. וּרְמִינְהִי: נִזְכַּר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת וְלֹא נִזְכַּר שָׁלִיחַ – הַשָּׁלִיחַ מָעַל, נִזְכְּרוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם – חֶנְוָנִי מָעַל!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If the homeowner «sent» the money «in the hand of» a halakhically «competent» person and the homeowner remembered that the money was consecrated before the agent reached the storekeeper, the storekeeper is liable for misuse when he spends the money for his personal use. This indicates that the storekeeper is liable «even though the agent did not remember,» but the homeowner alone remembered. «And» the Gemara «raises a contradiction» from a baraita: If «the homeowner remembered» that the money was consecrated, «but the agent did not remember, the agent is liable for misuse.» If «they both remembered» that the money is consecrated, the «storekeeper is liable for misuse.»
